items.headline: GetGo launches 'Drive to Malaysia', letting Singapore car-share users cross the Causeway
items.summary: GetGo, Singapore's largest car-sharing operator, switched on a 'Drive to Malaysia' feature on Sep 1 that lets members take its vehicles across the Causeway, with insurance and Malaysian charges handled through the app.

items.headline: Man jailed 22 years and given 24 strokes for raping his teenage stepdaughter
items.summary: A 43-year-old man was sentenced on Sep 1 to 22 years' jail and 24 strokes of the cane for repeatedly raping his stepdaughter, whom he began abusing when she was 16 and who was initially not believed by her family.

items.headline: ECDA to hire 1,800 more infant-care educators by 2030 with expanded grants
items.summary: The Early Childhood Development Agency said it will expand its Manpower Hiring Grant to bring in about 1,800 more infant-care educators by 2030, as demand for infant places rises.

items.headline: MTI to be renamed the Ministry of Energy, Trade and Industry from Oct 1
items.summary: The Ministry of Trade and Industry will become the Ministry of Energy, Trade and Industry from Oct 1, a change the government says reflects how central energy has become to Singapore's competitiveness and long-term resilience.

items.headline: India's economy grows a faster-than-expected 7.8% in the June quarter
items.summary: India's GDP expanded 7.8% year-on-year in the April-June quarter, beating forecasts and keeping it the fastest-growing major economy, with manufacturing, construction and services doing the heavy lifting and private investment showing early signs of stirring.

items.headline: The rupee climbs to a two-month high as the RBI sells dollars to defend it
items.summary: The rupee rose to a two-month high after the Reserve Bank of India, backed by record foreign-exchange reserves, sold dollars to steady the currency against pressure from higher oil prices.

items.headline: Modi urges 'dialogue and diplomacy' and presses Putin to end the Ukraine war at the SCO
items.summary: At the SCO summit in Bishkek, Prime Minister Narendra Modi renewed his call for 'dialogue and diplomacy', saying conflicts cannot be solved on the battlefield, and in a bilateral meeting urged President Vladimir Putin to end the war in Ukraine.

items.headline: Update: India's new closing auction absorbs a record $4.2 billion in MSCI rebalancing
items.summary: India's month-old closing-auction system cleared a record 4.2 billion dollars of trades tied to an MSCI index rebalancing on Monday. It handled the volume, but sharp swings in some stocks have traders calling for dedicated market makers.

items.headline: UK borrowing costs hit their highest since 1998, halving Burnham's fiscal headroom
items.summary: A global bond sell-off pushed the 30-year gilt yield to about 5.85%, its highest since 1998, roughly halving Chancellor John Healey's fiscal headroom and leaving him a reported £12 billion gap before his Oct 28 budget.

items.headline: Tensions over migrants and welfare set to test Burnham's Labour government
items.summary: Rows over migration and welfare are shaping up as an early test of Prime Minister Andy Burnham, with Labour caught between voters drifting to Reform UK and pressure from its own left over planned settlement and welfare curbs.

items.headline: Foreigners rush to secure UK residency before Burnham's settlement clampdown
items.summary: Foreign residents are rushing to secure permanent settlement and citizenship before the government tightens the rules, with applications spiking ahead of Burnham's planned clampdown on the path to UK residency.

items.headline: UK energy price cap to rise 4% to £1,723 in October as gas prices climb
items.summary: Ofgem said the energy price cap will rise about 4% to £1,723 a year from October, pushing household bills to their highest winter level since early 2024 as the Middle East conflict lifts wholesale gas prices and erodes Burnham's earlier VAT cut.

items.headline: US forces strike IRGC targets in Iran after attacks on Hormuz shipping
items.summary: US Central Command said American forces struck Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps targets in Iran on Sep 1, hitting sites near Chabahar, Konarak and the Strait of Hormuz in retaliation for an attempt to mine the strait and attacks on shipping. Iran vowed 'crushing' retaliation as Trump warned against it.

items.headline: SCO's Bishkek Declaration condemns strikes and sanctions on Iran as Xi and Putin reaffirm ties
items.summary: SCO leaders signed a 'Bishkek Declaration' at the bloc's 25th-anniversary summit condemning the strikes on Iran and Western sanctions on members, while Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin, meeting on the sidelines, said ties between Beijing and Moscow had grown 'more solid'.

items.headline: Update: Nepal-Tibet flood toll passes 1,000 with more than 4,000 still missing
items.summary: The death toll from the Himalayan glacier-collapse floods on the Nepal-Tibet border passed 1,000 on Sep 1, with more than 4,000 people still missing. Nepal has deployed 30,000 personnel and rescued about 1,550, while the count of unaccounted-for hydropower workers fell to 639.

items.headline: Israeli strikes kill at least five in Gaza as the post-ceasefire toll passes 1,300
items.summary: Israeli strikes killed at least five people across Gaza on Aug 31, including near a park in Gaza City, as diplomats pressed a stalled deal to disarm Hamas and withdraw Israeli troops. Monitors say more than 1,300 Palestinians have been killed since the US-brokered ceasefire took effect.

items.headline: John Ternus takes over as Apple CEO and teases a 'huge launch next week'
items.summary: John Ternus has taken over as Apple's chief executive, succeeding Tim Cook after 15 years, and used his first company memo to tease a 'huge launch next week' ahead of the Sep 9 iPhone event expected to unveil Apple's first foldable.

items.headline: Anthropic strikes a $35 billion cloud deal with Nvidia-backed Lambda
items.summary: Anthropic agreed a $35 billion cloud-computing deal with Nvidia-backed Lambda, tapping a new Texas data centre developed by Hut 8, as the AI company races to expand capacity following a string of multibillion-dollar compute pacts.

items.headline: Andreessen Horowitz's growth fund swells to $8.5 billion after a fresh $1.1bn raise
items.summary: Andreessen Horowitz has expanded its latest growth fund to $8.5 billion, days after closing a separate $1.1 billion 'Machine Age Fund', underscoring how much capital continues to pour into AI and its infrastructure.

items.headline: CrowdStrike tops estimates and adds security deals as AI lifts cyber demand
items.summary: CrowdStrike beat fiscal second-quarter estimates with adjusted earnings of 31 cents a share on $1.47 billion in revenue and raised its outlook, arguing AI is boosting security demand. It also announced about $740 million in deals for startups SGNL and Pangea.

items.headline: US stocks slide as Treasury yields hit multiyear highs and Fed hike bets grow
items.summary: US stocks fell to start September, with the S&P 500 down 0.71% to 7,631.47, the Dow off 419 points to 52,766.88 and the Nasdaq down 1.03%, as a global bond sell-off lifted yields to multiyear highs and futures priced a 68% chance of a Fed rate hike.

items.headline: Oil jumps above $94 after US strikes on Iran rattle the Strait of Hormuz
items.summary: Oil climbed above $94 a barrel, with Brent up nearly 4%, after US Central Command announced fresh strikes on Iran near the Strait of Hormuz. OPEC+ is due to meet on Sep 6.

items.headline: Gold tumbles about 2% to a two-week low as yields and the dollar climb
items.summary: Gold dropped about 2% to a two-week low near $4,360 an ounce as rising Treasury yields and a firmer dollar overwhelmed safe-haven demand, pushing bullion below its 200-day moving average.

items.headline: Bond traders rush to hedge as Treasury yields approach multiyear highs
items.summary: Bond investors are paying up for protection as the global debt sell-off deepens, with one trade this week wagering $6.5 million that the 30-year US Treasury yield climbs toward 5.7% by November.

items.headline: Djokovic suffers his first Grand Slam opening-round exit since 2006, beaten by Navone
items.summary: Novak Djokovic suffered his first opening-round exit at a Grand Slam since the 2006 Australian Open, beaten 7-6(5), 5-7, 4-6, 6-2, 6-1 by Argentina's Mariano Navone, 25, at the US Open. Djokovic was visibly ailing and was sick on court late in the match.

items.headline: Alcaraz returns from a wrist injury with a straight-sets US Open win over Safiullin
items.summary: Defending champion Carlos Alcaraz eased back from a four-month wrist injury, beating Roman Safiullin 6-4, 6-4, 6-4 in the US Open first round to improve to 8-0 at the majors in 2026.

items.headline: Sabalenka opens her US Open title defence with a straight-sets win over Osorio
items.summary: Two-time defending champion Aryna Sabalenka opened her US Open title bid with a 6-4, 6-4 win over Camila Osorio, as the top seed began a campaign for a third straight New York title.

items.headline: India and Pakistan head for a Women's Asia Cup group showdown on Sept 5
items.summary: India and Pakistan are set to meet in the Women's T20 Asia Cup group stage in Dubai on Sep 5, one of the tournament's marquee fixtures, after India opened its campaign with a 94-run rout of Thailand.

items.headline: Formula 1's title fight arrives at Monza for the Italian Grand Prix
items.summary: Formula 1 heads to Monza for the Italian Grand Prix on Sep 6, where championship leader Kimi Antonelli — 59 points clear — will start near the back after taking a new power unit, while Lando Norris arrives on a two-win streak, 83 points behind.

items.headline: A gene therapy that ferries interferon into tumours shows early promise against glioblastoma
items.summary: In a phase 1/2 trial, 24 patients with newly diagnosed glioblastoma received Temferon, a genetically engineered stem-cell therapy that delivers interferon-alpha into the tumour's microenvironment. It was well tolerated, with stable engraftment and early signs of immune reprogramming.

items.headline: A Chinese fusion reactor pushes its plasma past a key density threshold
items.summary: Physicists reported that a Chinese fusion reactor pushed its plasma past a crucial density threshold, a milestone toward the stable, high-density conditions that a future fusion power plant would need.

items.headline: Study finds most ocean species are shifting range and behaviour as seas warm
items.summary: A study compiling more than 1,700 long-term observations of marine life, from plankton to polar bears, found about 80% showed shifts in range, timing or behaviour consistent with a warming ocean, with plankton among the biggest movers.

items.headline: Scientists recover human DNA locked in ancient cave paintings
items.summary: Researchers recovered human DNA preserved in ancient cave paintings in Spain and Portugal, suggesting decorated caves can act as long-term 'genetic archives' and offering a new, non-destructive way to study the people who made prehistoric art.

fun_fact.headline: Some red food dye is made from crushed cochineal insects
fun_fact.body: That vivid red in some sweets, yogurts, and lipsticks can come from insects. Carmine — also labelled cochineal or E120 — is a crimson dye made by crushing and boiling the dried bodies of the cochineal, a scale insect farmed on prickly-pear cacti. It takes roughly 70,000 of them to make a single pound of the dye, which has coloured food and fabric since the time of the Aztecs.
fun_fact.source: Encyclopaedia Britannica; US Food and Drug Administration

puzzle.title: Six Matches, Four Triangles
puzzle.body: You have six identical matchsticks. Arrange all six so that they form exactly four equilateral triangles, every side exactly one match long. You may not break, bend, or cross the matches. How?
puzzle.approach: Count how many triangles you can make flat on a table, then ask what changes if you stop thinking in two dimensions.
puzzle.answer: Build a tetrahedron (a triangular pyramid). Lay three matches flat to make one triangle, then stand the remaining three upright from the three corners so they meet at a single point above the centre. The pyramid's four faces — the base plus three sides — are each an equilateral triangle with one-match edges. It cannot be done flat on the table; you must build upward into three dimensions.

word_puzzle.title: Worth Noting
word_puzzle.body: Centre letter T (required in every word); other letters A, B, E, L, N, O. Make as many words as you can (4+ letters), each using only these seven letters — letters may repeat — and each containing T. One word, the pangram, uses all seven letters at least once.
word_puzzle.approach: Every word must contain the centre letter and use only the seven letters shown; letters may repeat. One word — the pangram — uses all seven.
word_puzzle.answer: Pangram: NOTABLE (uses A, B, E, L, N, O, T). Other valid words include BEAT, BOAT, BOLT, BLOT, BELT, NOTE, TONE, ANTE, ONTO, TOTE, TABLE, TALON, TONAL, TOTAL, BATON, LATTE, BLOAT, BOTTLE, TALENT, BATTLE, ABLATE, OBLATE, TABLET, BLATANT.
